title: Pasting invertible scalar mates through exact derived localization
statement: Let A,B,C,D,E,F be abelian categories with ordinary unbounded derived categories. Let R0:B→A, R1:D→C, R2:F→E and U01:A→C, U12:C→E, U02:A→E, V01:B→D, V12:D→F, V02:B→F be additive exact functors. Specify adjunctions Li left adjoint to the exact derived Ri. Let kij:Ri followed by Uij be naturally isomorphic to Vij followed by Rj. Let cU:U02≅U01 followed by U12 and cV:V02≅V01 followed by V12 satisfy k02(N);R2(cV(N))=cU(R0N);U12(k01(N));k12(V01N). If the inverse mates of the localized k01 and k12 are invertible, the inverse mate of localized k02 is invertible.

source.place: Tags 05S7 and 014F, localization of exact functor squares, followed by elementary adjunction mate pasting.

proof.text: Apply exact-square composition under unbounded derived localization to the ordinary component equation. This gives the corresponding identity with derived compositors obtained from cU and cV. Cancel the invertible cV compositor to identify the localized total square with the specified pasted square.

Form the horizontal paste of the inverse mates of the two constituent squares. Whisker by cU and cV inverse. The mate of this whiskered square is the vertical paste of the original squares, with those same compositors: naturality of the adjunction unit and naturality of cV give the whiskering equation, and mateEquiv_vcomp gives the pasting equation. The derived identity from step one identifies its mate with the specified total square. Since mateEquiv is a bijection, this whiskered paste is the total inverse mate. All its factors are invertible, so it is invertible.

proof_origin.place: Exact-localization universal property and elementary adjunction mate pasting; full Lean proof.

theorem derivedScalarMatePasting
    {A B C D E F : Type*}
    [Category A] [Category B] [Category C] [Category D] [Category E] [Category F]
    [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [Abelian C] [Abelian D] [Abelian E] [Abelian F]
    [HasDerivedCategory A] [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasDerivedCategory C]
    [HasDerivedCategory D] [HasDerivedCategory E] [HasDerivedCategory F]
    (R₀ : B ⥤ A) (R₁ : D ⥤ C) (R₂ : F ⥤ E)
    (U₀₁ : A ⥤ C) (U₁₂ : C ⥤ E) (U₀₂ : A ⥤ E)
    (V₀₁ : B ⥤ D) (V₁₂ : D ⥤ F) (V₀₂ : B ⥤ F)
    [R₀.Additive] [R₁.Additive] [R₂.Additive]
    [U₀₁.Additive] [U₁₂.Additive] [U₀₂.Additive]
    [V₀₁.Additive] [V₁₂.Additive] [V₀₂.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits R₀] [PreservesFiniteColimits R₀]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits R₁] [PreservesFiniteColimits R₁]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits R₂] [PreservesFiniteColimits R₂]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits U₀₁] [PreservesFiniteColimits U₀₁]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits U₁₂] [PreservesFiniteColimits U₁₂]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits U₀₂] [PreservesFiniteColimits U₀₂]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits V₀₁] [PreservesFiniteColimits V₀₁]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits V₁₂] [PreservesFiniteColimits V₁₂]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits V₀₂] [PreservesFiniteColimits V₀₂]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits (U₀₁ ⋙ U₁₂)] [PreservesFiniteColimits (U₀₁ ⋙ U₁₂)]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits (V₀₁ ⋙ V₁₂)] [PreservesFiniteColimits (V₀₁ ⋙ V₁₂)]
    {L₀ : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory B}
    {L₁ : DerivedCategory C ⥤ DerivedCategory D}
    {L₂ : DerivedCategory E ⥤ DerivedCategory F}
    (a₀ : L₀ ⊣ R₀.mapDerivedCategory) (a₁ : L₁ ⊣ R₁.mapDerivedCategory)
    (a₂ : L₂ ⊣ R₂.mapDerivedCategory)
    (k₀₁ : R₀ ⋙ U₀₁ ≅ V₀₁ ⋙ R₁) (k₁₂ : R₁ ⋙ U₁₂ ≅ V₁₂ ⋙ R₂)
    (k₀₂ : R₀ ⋙ U₀₂ ≅ V₀₂ ⋙ R₂)
    (cU : U₀₂ ≅ U₀₁ ⋙ U₁₂) (cV : V₀₂ ≅ V₀₁ ⋙ V₁₂)
    (hk : ∀ N, k₀₂.hom.app N ≫ R₂.map (cV.hom.app N) =
      cU.hom.app (R₀.obj N) ≫ U₁₂.map (k₀₁.hom.app N) ≫ k₁₂.hom.app (V₀₁.obj N))
    (h₀₁ : IsIso ((mateEquiv a₀ a₁).symm
      (Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso k₀₁).hom).natTrans)
    (h₁₂ : IsIso ((mateEquiv a₁ a₂).symm
      (Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso k₁₂).hom).natTrans) :
    IsIso ((mateEquiv a₀ a₂).symm
      (Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso k₀₂).hom).natTrans
